messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: API Naming/Organization
parts:
As we continue refactoring we have come to the point where we want to formalize the interaction with the internal Stan code and the code implemented by the interfaces.

From a client/service perspective we have two sets of relationships: Stan provides services for the client interfaces, and the interfaces provide implementations of classes (mostly I/O) that can be thought of as services with Stan the client. The question is how formally we want to stick to this kind of pattern, if at all.

1) Ultimately this requires renaming and reorganizing the infamous “common” directory (not as infamous as “gm”, but that can come later). Putting everything into a single “services” folder can be confusing, but how about

src/services (common classes for the interfaces to call)
src/interface (base classes defining what the interfaces need to implement)

2) How deeply can interface code interact with internal Stan code? For example, lots of code in src/mcmc needs somewhere to dump output and messages. An immediate answer is to template everything with a Recorder class which gets implemented by the interfaces. But do we want code outside of services to use such classes (even if they’re templated)? Or do we want some intermediary structure that keeps the use of such classes in, say, src/services?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] API Naming/Organization
parts:
On Sep 4, 2014, at 5:16 PM, Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com> wrote:

> As we continue refactoring we have come to the point where we want to formalize the interaction with the internal Stan code and the code implemented by the interfaces.
>
> From a client/service perspective we have two sets of relationships: Stan provides services for the client interfaces, and the interfaces provide implementations of classes (mostly I/O) that can be thought of as services with Stan the client. The question is how formally we want to stick to this kind of pattern, if at all.

This kind of callback setup should be general enough for
the I/O abstractions we need now.

> 1) Ultimately this requires renaming and reorganizing the infamous "common" directory (not as infamous as "gm", but that can come later). Putting everything into a single "services" folder can be confusing, but how about
>
> src/services (common classes for the interfaces to call)
> src/interface (base classes defining what the interfaces need to implement)

So you think not under src/stan? I think that'd be OK.

I now see why you wanted to use src/api for src/interface.
I think either would be OK. As would src/client (but that's
more named after who uses than what it provides, so I prefer
the former).

> 2) How deeply can interface code interact with internal Stan code? For example, lots of code in src/mcmc needs somewhere to dump output and messages. An immediate answer is to template everything with a Recorder class which gets implemented by the interfaces. But do we want code outside of services to use such classes (even if they're templated)? Or do we want some intermediary structure that keeps the use of such classes in, say, src/services?

As deep as it wants.

What I wanted to prevent is includes from src/stan into
src/services or src/interface. So some of what you think
of as src/interface may be classes within Stan. Such as
the mcmc_writer.

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] API Naming/Organization
parts:
Classes that have to be implemented by each interface, such as recorder, get moved into interface.

Classes/functions that provide common resources for the interfaces, such as warmup and sample, get moved into services.

The idea is that each interface should only have to implement a few classes in interface (recorder, var_context_factory, callback)
and then everything else can be used by templating out these implementations.

move where..

Best,
